prompt:
Create ONE substantially repainted character illustration using the two references with strictly different roles.

REFERENCE ROLES
Image 1, the Sdorica Sione illustration, is the PRIMARY reference for the painting language: designed connected color planes, selective colored linework, broad curved metal forms, restrained reflectivity, and a deliberate hierarchy of hard, soft and understated edges. Study the main adult figure only. Do not copy its white hair, silver-blue costume, pose, chibi, lettering, pedestal, grainy halo, or background.
Image 2 is the content and action reference for OUR adult red-haired archer. Retain her recognizable identity, crimson high ponytail, warm amber eyes, violet-and-gold outfit, currently exposed upper arms/shoulders and upper thighs, bow and arrow, and the same dramatic low full-draw action. Its shiny rendering, equal-strength outlines, repeated hair ribbons and evenly emphasized gold trim are precisely what must be replaced. This needs a visibly new art treatment and shape organization, not another smoothing filter on image 2.

CHARACTER AND ACTION
One adult woman, about 25, an elegant athletic fantasy archer. Preserve the reference's three-quarter torso, face looking toward the target to image right, extended bow arm toward image right, string hand anchored beside her face on image left, near leg reaching diagonally toward the bottom right and far leg folded toward the left. Keep the forceful low pose, coherent shoulder girdle, ribcage, pelvis, knees and ankles, continuous limb anatomy and readable hands. The bowstring is ONE continuous string between the two bow tips, deflected to the arrow nock at the drawing hand. The single arrow rests correctly at the bow and aligns with her aim. Keep the entire character, feet and bow inside a vertical canvas with a modest clear margin.

PRIMARY VISUAL CHANGE: WHOLE-FIGURE ORGANIZATION
Organize one coherent illuminated region across the face, upper chest, drawing hand and nearby shoulder, and broad connected shadow families through the remaining torso, hair underside, skirt and legs. Adjacent parts share the same light environment; they do not each receive their own miniature highlight-and-shadow showcase. Face and drawing action are the focal point. Lower legs, shoe tips, skirt lining and peripheral hair remain readable but quieter. Remove the bright white triangular glare on the front shoe and other competing accessory highlights. Do not darken everything into mud or fade the body away.

PAINTING METHOD FROM IMAGE 1
A finished 2D fantasy character painting with a classical decorative storybook sensibility. Build the forms from intact local-color areas and a few substantial, deliberately shaped light, turning and shadow planes. Allow subtle soft changes within broad curved planes. Preserve decisive edges where form turns or pieces overlap, with quieter edges elsewhere. The result must feel drawn and painted through shape decisions, not photorealistic, sculpted 3D, an airbrushed plastic render or a flat unshaded vector. No randomized triangulated patches, no 'faded dye' mottling, no noisy brush fragments. Continuous color does not mean blurring every transition.

FACE AND HAIR
Keep the archer's warm recognizable adult face and amber eye color. Use clear slightly elongated eye shapes, a selective upper eyelid line, an understated mouth and nose, compact continuous skin planes, very restrained blush and eye glints. Her expression is focused, intelligent and composed.
Reorganize the crimson high ponytail into one dominant directional sweep with a few subordinate masses of visibly different widths and lengths. Slightly reduce its excessive ballooning so the face commands attention, while preserving the long dynamic silhouette. Give the hair plausible flow from the tie, taper and clear overlap. Replace the repeated equal-size rolled loops and parallel ribbon stacks. Carry broad connected red light and dark shapes across multiple locks; use local fine lines only at important separations. Rich crimson and vermilion in lit areas, coherent deeper red in shadow, not a highlight stripe on every strand. Controlled asymmetry and a few purposeful loose strands.

COSTUME SHAPES AND MATERIALS
Maintain the violet-and-gold archer design and its present tasteful exposure. Keep substantial designed clothing and functional armor: fitted violet bodice, attached broad skirt panels, leather belt and gloves, shaped shoulder plates, bracers and leg guards. Garments and armor have credible attachment and thickness. Let the bodice read as one constructed garment following the ribcage, not separately polished inflated spherical cups.
Violet cloth: stable, saturated violet local color, a few large folds with clear tension or compression at the belt and skirt attachments, continuous planes and modest soft transitions. Broad hem panels remain intact. Make the pale lining a subordinate warm ivory in the shared shadow, not a brilliant white fan.
Gold armor: broad curved plates whose shape and overlapping thickness carry the design. Use connected warm gold/ochre body color and a few large warm/cool reflected planes, much like image 1's metal method translated into gold. Use only a few selective narrow highlights at focal structural turns. Reduce mirror reflections, jagged glare and perimeter-wide bright gold borders. Each knee guard or shoe must not become a separate jewel-like focal point.
Concentrate meaningful ornaments near shoulder/chest and the belt clasp; integrate a small number of curved engraved motifs into the surfaces. Simplify repeated leaf spikes, hooks and gold zigzags at every joint without stripping all character design. Leave large readable quiet planes between decorated regions. Dark leather remains one coherent material, not mottled strips.

COLOR AND EDGES
Preserve the vivid crimson, rich violet and warm gold identity requested by the user. Borrow the reference's color relationships and painting method, not its overall gray palette. No global desaturation. Warm skin is distinct from cloth and metal; cooler reflected colors appear sparingly inside the shared shadows.
Use thin colored linework only where it clarifies eyelids, hair overlap, plate joints, a few engraved curves and necessary cloth folds. Do not outline every part in the same dark line or illuminate every edge. Keep the alpha silhouette clean and fully present while varying painted contour strength. Preserve a fine, quiet painted surface without covering the subject in paper grain, scratches, stippling or watercolor noise.

DELIVERY
One complete standalone character cutout, genuinely transparent alpha background and transparent gaps between hair, limbs and bow. No colored haze or glow, no ground, architecture, clouds, dust, painterly backdrop, pedestal, particles, typography, labels, chibi or comparison panels. Do not copy the black or colored RGB behind transparent areas of either reference. Only one final image.
